title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page sets up a standard truncation formalism for a category M of graded objects with a differential. From τ_N(P)_i = P_i for i ≥ N, 0 for i < N, being a subobject of P, these are most plausibly cochain complexes, with d raising degree. In context (cote 136, divided-power de Rham complex) they are probably complexes of modules, or of crystals/filtered objects, of de Rham type.

Notation:
- M_N is the full subcategory of objects concentrated in degrees ≥ N.
- M^N is the full subcategory of objects concentrated in degrees ≤ N.

(9)-(9.3) record the inclusion functors i_N : M_N → M and i^N : M^N → M. For N ≤ N' there are transition inclusions i_{N,N'} : M_{N'} → M_N and i^{N';N} : M^N → M^{N'}. These satisfy the obvious transitivity relations.

Proposition 1 states that i_N sits in a chain of four adjoint functors q_N ⊣ i_N ⊣ τ_N ⊣ φ_N.
- τ_N is the 'stupid' truncation σ_{≥N}. It is the largest subobject of P lying in M_N, and the counit i_N τ_N(P) → P is the adjunction arrow ('flèche d'adjonction').
- q_N, the left adjoint, is presumably the quotient truncation: Coker(d: P_{N-1} → P_N) in degree N and P_i for i > N (the canonical truncation τ_{≥N}).
- φ_N, the right adjoint of τ_N, is presumably Q ↦ (Q_N →id→ Q_N → Q_{N+1} → …), with Q_N placed in degree N-1. One checks Hom(σ_{≥N}P, Q) ≅ Hom(P, φ_N Q): the degree N-1 component is forced to be f_N ∘ d.

The sequel would treat the dual chain for i^N. The purpose is likely to organise truncations, e.g. of Hodge/conjugate filtrations on the divided-power de Rham complex, as adjoint functors.

The page is written on the back of a typescript page of SGA 7 exposé IX (semi-stable reduction, monodromy pairing); that text is unrelated to the handwritten content.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. The definitions of q_N and φ_N are announced but not yet written, so their exact form is inferred.
There is minor notational inconsistency between i^{N';N} in (9.1) and 'i^N, i^{N,N'}' in the later sentence.

ideas.what: Chain of four adjoint functors q_N ⊣ i_N ⊣ τ_N ⊣ φ_N attached to the inclusion of complexes concentrated in degrees ≥ N, with τ_N the stupid truncation
ideas.modern_name: adjoint string of truncation functors / stupid vs canonical truncations as adjoints to inclusion
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (homological algebra; cf. Deligne's treatment of truncations in Hodge II and t-structures in BBD for derived-category analogues)

ideas.what: Transitivity of inclusions M_{N''} ⊂ M_{N'} ⊂ M_N and M^N ⊂ M^{N'} ⊂ M^{N''}

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains routine categorical bookkeeping about truncation functors on complexes and their adjoint strings. It is standard and nothing on it appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'flèche d'adjonction' rather than 'plus grand sous-objet d'adjonction': the label under τ_N(P) ⊂ P refers to the adjunction arrow i_N τ_N(P) → P.
In Proposition 1 the inserted text reads 'i_N : M_N ↪ M s'insère dans une suite de 4 foncteurs adjoints'.
The first functor in (10) is probably q_N; the handwriting is ambiguous ('9N').
Line (10.1) reads 'τ_N(P) ⊂ P (sous objet de P)', with an equality sign below identifying it with i_N τ_N(P).
'(foncteur troncature à droite)' appears to be the correct reading of the annotation next to τ_N.
The struck-out words before (9.2) are 'On va étudier les', followed by 'donc on a'. The struck 'plus' before 'et si N ≤ N' ≤ N''' is correct.
